attempts.summary: Built a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL7) serving AMQP strictly over TLS on port 5671 with mutual TLS enforced against a cluster-dedicated CA, and restricted the management UI (15672) to the cluster-internal network. Erlang 28.5.0.5 and RabbitMQ 4.3.5 were installed from the official zero-dependency EL7 GitHub release RPMs (RHEL7 had no configured yum repos and upstream no longer ships EL7 packages/repo). A private CA was generated on node1 with per-node server certs (SAN=hostname+cluster IP) and a client cert; rabbitmq.conf disables plaintext AMQP (listeners.tcp = none), enables listeners.ssl on 5671 with ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, and binds management.tcp.ip to each node's private cluster IP (10.100.9.x) with firewalld further restricting 15672/25672/4369 to the 10.100.9.0/24 subnet. All 3 nodes clustered automatically via classic_config peer discovery sharing one Erlang cookie. Verified: TLS connections without a client cert or with a non-CA (rogue) cert are rejected at the handshake; a CA-issued client cert completes the handshake and receives a real AMQP Connection.Start frame; a full publish/get message round-trip succeeded via the management API. Also fixed significant clock drift (~9 days) on all 3 nodes via chrony/date, which was blocking TLS cert validation for package downloads. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified RabbitMQ became active, full 3/3 cluster quorum returned, and TLS/mTLS enforcement plus message publish/consume worked after each restart, before moving to the next node.
